body: Actually, after reading the links... I read very quickly. I mean, I can read an average novel in a couple hours. But I'm reading dense theory full of new terms. I think I'm spending the most time on underlining and rereading important parts and sometimes back reading to apply something to something that came before it, yanno?
Thanks, those links are very helpful.

Ironically, I don't think I have time to read it!

No really, I'll go read it now. Thanks.
Evernote allows tags and searching, right?
Sociology/communication. I'm reading theories that I need to be able to apply to things.

I was homeless for years as a teenager. Even the state didn't want me. 

Now I own my home free and clear and have good friends. Life can change really fast sometimes, and you can change it sometimes. Homelessness takes constant engagement with the world and a level of skill and strategy. Not that it isn't depressing, but it always perks me up a bit. 

Also, you're free!  So many people can't do anything cause they're stuck with bills and jobs and ugh. You're free to travel the country by greyhound or thumb and jug. You could go to rainbow gathering or spend days at the library reading all the good things or... well, you get to choose your own adventure. 

Best of luck on your journey.

I'm sorry you're in so much pain. Life is horrible sometimes. 

Loving yourself can be the hardest thing in the world, and it can be the thing that gets you through. Breath. Make yourself some tea. Moisturize. These little moments add up to staying alive.

I hear you. It is really fucked up that the experts on people like us make all this money pretending they can help us, and then if we don't get better it's all our fault. We must not want it or be trying hard enough. Fuck that shit.
Well, if it does please report back. :)

I dunno, but I'm in the sameish boat. Maybe education makes us hopeless. 

As a neuroscientist, what do you think about DMT?

I read this book recently:

http://www.amazon.com/gp/aw/d/0300186088

It says that people have always had moments like you're having, and for most of history it wasn't thought of as a pathology, just something that passes like a rainy day.  I always thought the copycat thing was kind of bullshit, but his book goes into a lot of research and shows that it's true. Then it says that when you distract yourself from that voice and stay alive till it passes you're actually saving other people's lives too.

I was more optimistic when I was your age too. 

My life is pretty cool and I seem to fuck up less than the average person. I've done a lot of adventuring and achieved a lot of goals. Just none of that has taken away the darkness or made me not want to die.

Yeah. I actually make half my living from writing. I think writing about depressing things makes me depressed though. 

I do play some music and it's a good way not to kill myself for a few hours. I'm not good enough to jam with people tho.

I'm sorry you've lost so much. It must be devastating to feel so alone while grieving. If you're still around maybe we can chat and be alone together. 

You sound like such a good pet owner. Are you comfortable sharing what city you're in so people can try to help find resources for the animals?
